plants.name: Groot
plants.searchName: groot ponytail palm elephant foot tree
plants.photoAlt: Groot · Ponytail palm · photo review Oct 12, 2026

sections.label: NEXT ACTION
sections.bodyHtml: No urgent care changes indicated. Keep in strong light, checking that the mix has dried throughout before watering thoroughly and draining. Protect from persistently wet soil. The curling leaf shape is normal for ponytail palm; no trimming needed other than fully dead tips if desired.

sections.label: CURRENT CONDITION
sections.bodyHtml: Nov 4, 2026 chat photograph compared with Oct 12 GAIA cover: dense crown of narrow, arching, naturally curling green leaves, with an established, swollen, firm-looking elephant-foot trunk. A few older leaf bends or small scuffs are visible without widespread yellowing or obvious pest clusters. Overall foliage appears healthy and stable; different lighting and angle do not support an exact new-leaf count or a definite density increase. Actual trunk firmness, roots and soil moisture have not been physically checked.

sections.label: WATER
sections.bodyHtml: Groot is in a self-watering wick pot. Do not maintain a continuously full reservoir: allow the substrate to dry all the way through between waterings, and leave reservoir empty during dry-down. Check moisture below the surface, not just at the top. Water thoroughly when dry, then remove any standing water.

sections.label: LIGHT
sections.bodyHtml: Brightest available window with direct sun; increase stronger sunlight gradually to prevent scorching.

sections.label: FERTILIZER
sections.bodyHtml: No immediate feeding. Fertilize once or twice during active spring–summer growth at the product’s label rate; skip while stressed or resting.

sections.label: LOCATION
sections.bodyHtml: Table beside the window shown in the photo; window direction and final placement not recorded.

sections.label: REPOT
sections.bodyHtml: Owner is considering moving Groot from his wick pot into a standard draining pot, then reusing the wick pot for a moisture-loving plant. Not yet repotted. Since Groot looks healthy, there is no urgency unless the wick setup keeps roots wet. When moving, use a similarly sized pot with drainage, a freely draining gritty mix, and keep the swollen caudex above the soil line; minimize root disturbance. Spring is a reasonable time if conditions remain stable.

sections.label: SOIL
sections.bodyHtml: Fast-draining cactus/succulent mix with added perlite or pumice; a 1:1 mix is a practical starting point. Use a pot with drainage and keep the swollen trunk above the mix.

sections.label: WATCH
sections.bodyHtml: Monitor for persistent soil wetness or a genuinely soft trunk/base, widespread new yellowing, or new pest activity. Ordinary curling and pre-existing leaf creases are cosmetic and need no intervention. Check young center leaves over time for healthy growth.

sections.label: PROPAGATION
sections.bodyHtml: Usually grown from seed. Leaf cuttings will not make a new plant; leave attached shoots in place.

sections.label: PEST CHECK
sections.bodyHtml: No infestation confirmed from the photo. Keep apart from affected plants during any active mite outbreak and check leaf bases and undersides.

plants.name: Audrey II
plants.photoAlt: Audrey II · Venus flytrap · photo review Oct 12, 2026

sections.label: NEXT ACTION
sections.bodyHtml: Oct 13: Reece reported the medium was very dry and began a bottom-soak in the original nursery pot (drainage holes confirmed). Verify that the center of the medium is rehydrated; do not mark the soak finished until Reece confirms. Switch to distilled, reverse-osmosis, or clean rainwater as soon as available, and keep moist. Leave Audrey II by the bright window and grow light with the succulents while recovering. Check the bedroom east-window sill temperature before planning a cool winter rest.

sections.label: CURRENT CONDITION
sections.bodyHtml: Oct 13 photo: several green traps and green central growth remain, alongside older blackening traps and dry surface material. Reece confirmed severe dryness and began rehydration. Dehydration is a concern; the cause of blackening and lack of trap response is not established. Monitor new traps and recovery rather than repeatedly triggering traps.

sections.label: WATER
sections.bodyHtml: Keep the low-nutrient medium consistently moist using distilled, reverse-osmosis, or clean rainwater (ideally very low dissolved minerals). A single emergency tap-water soaking is generally less risky than leaving it severely dry, but tap water should not become the routine; whether tap water was actually used Oct 13 is unconfirmed. While actively growing, a shallow tray of about 1–2 cm water is suitable; ensure the pot drains. During a truly cool winter rest, keep the medium just moist rather than waterlogged.

sections.label: LIGHT
sections.bodyHtml: Usual position: a bright window with a grow light, next to the succulents. Strong light is appropriate while growing and recovering (roughly 6+ hours direct sun after acclimation, or a sufficiently strong grow light for about 12–16 hours daily). The alternate bedroom window faces east and gets morning sun; this reduced light is only an option for a genuinely cool dormant plant, not reliable active growth at room temperature.

sections.label: FERTILIZER
sections.bodyHtml: No standard fertilizer in the soil or water. Do not force-feed while it is stressed or traps are unresponsive; later, healthy growing traps can receive suitable small insects.

sections.label: LOCATION
sections.bodyHtml: Usual home: window with supplemental grow light alongside succulents (window direction not confirmed). Possible winter home: directly on the east-facing bedroom windowsill, with morning sun. Bedroom sill temperatures have not been measured; user reports the current growing location stays near room temperature.

sections.label: REPOT
sections.bodyHtml: Currently in the small original nursery pot, which has drainage holes. Do not repot immediately while dehydrated; first allow the medium to rehydrate and the plant to stabilize. Nursery medium composition is unverified. Consider a spring repot only if needed; use unfertilized carnivorous-plant medium, not standard potting soil.

sections.label: SOIL
sections.bodyHtml: Unfertilized long-fiber sphagnum, or a carnivorous-plant mix such as unfertilized sphagnum peat with washed silica sand. No standard potting mix or fertilizer-enriched ingredients.

sections.label: WATCH
sections.bodyHtml: After the Oct 13 rehydration, check for renewed growth and adequate moisture through the center of the pot. Older traps may blacken naturally; trim only fully dead, easy-to-remove material. Do not manually trigger traps to test them. Verify actual water source and window temperatures. Keep apart from plants showing active spider mites; no mites established on Audrey II.

sections.label: PROPAGATION
sections.bodyHtml: Divide established plants during a suitable repot; leaf pullings and seed are also possible. Wait until this plant is stable.

sections.label: PEST CHECK
sections.bodyHtml: No infestation confirmed from this photo. Keep separate during the collection’s mite follow-up. Reece confirms no bath and no watering since receiving it; previous water quality remains unknown.

sections.label: WINTER PLAN
sections.bodyHtml: Oct 13 plan: prioritize recovery under the existing strong window/grow light. Measure overnight temperatures on the east-facing bedroom windowsill before any move. A cool, bright winter rest is typically best (approximately 35–55°F / 2–13°C, with no hard freezing of this small pot). If the sill stays at ordinary room temperature, morning-only sun is insufficient for active growth; keep the strong grow light and reassess winter options rather than forcing dormancy. While genuinely dormant, use less water but never allow the medium to dry completely.

sections.bodyHtml: Do not rush to fertilize newly rooting cuttings. Once root establishment and continued growth are evident, feed sparingly in active growth following product directions.

sections.label: LOCATION
sections.bodyHtml: Three small pots on a metal grow-light shelf, photographed Nov 4. Final or permanent arrangement not recorded.

sections.label: REPOT
sections.bodyHtml: All three remain in individual small nursery containers. Pot up individually only after good root establishment and when roots need more room; avoid oversized wet containers.

sections.label: SOIL
sections.bodyHtml: Perlite-and-bark propagation material was previously reported. Current pots have coarse, pale material at the surface; exact full mix is not confirmed. Maintain airy, freely draining substrate.

sections.label: WATCH
sections.bodyHtml: Check for healthy new leaves at each crown, whether drying stays confined to older basal leaves, and whether stems or bases become soft. Some fibrous curls can be normal yucca leaf filaments. Note progress individually after assigning names to pots.

dashboardTasks.title: Inspect the six plants with reported mites
dashboardTasks.detail: Check leaf undersides and stem joints on Morgana, Phil, C-3PO, Tywin, Karlach and Calcifer for webbing or moving mites.

dashboardTasks.title: Repeat the white-paper mite test
dashboardTasks.detail: Recheck affected plants and the palm; look for tiny moving specks.

dashboardTasks.title: Inspect new arrivals and maintain separation
dashboardTasks.detail: Look for mite activity before placing newcomers beside plants from the affected group.

dashboardTasks.title: Check Audrey II’s rehydration and distilled water
dashboardTasks.detail: Soak began Oct 13 after very dry medium. Confirm the pot has rehydrated and soaking is finished, then maintain moist medium using distilled, reverse-osmosis, or clean rainwater. Do not mark watering complete without confirmation.

dashboardTasks.title: Check Bowser and the ponytail palm before watering
dashboardTasks.detail: Confirm drainage and wait until the mix is dry throughout; don’t water them on the tropical-plant schedule.

dashboardTasks.title: Review any repeat mite treatment
dashboardTasks.detail: If you are using a spray treatment, repeat only at the product label’s specified interval.

dashboardTasks.title: Measure Audrey II’s bedroom windowsill temperature
dashboardTasks.detail: Check the east-facing bedroom sill overnight before relocating Audrey II for winter. A cool spot (~35–55°F) may support dormancy; if it stays near room temperature, continue strong supplemental lighting and reassess. Protect the pot from freezing.
